[^2]: Module usage notice: `rounds=[# of iterations] is optional here, after signature, e.g. $5$rounds=5000`
[^3]: Module advice notice: `When using the optimized-kernel: some byte encoding is simplified that would make some non-ASCII passwords never be cracked, even if they are under the optimized byte limit. The pure-kernel implements true UTF16 handling so doesn't have this problem and should crack all passwords.`
[^4]: Module usage notice: `Use tools/encfs2hashcat.py on the encrypted directory or its .encfs6.xml to extract the hash. Only AES volumes are supported`
[^5]: Module usage notice: `Use tools/openssl2hashcat.py to extract the hash. A line that checks only the padding is refused, because the padding alone lets one wrong password in 255 through: pass -p with at least 5 bytes of text the file is known to contain, or -a with a minimum share of printable ASCII. The share a line needs falls as it carries more data, from 85 percent at 48 bytes to 55 percent at 256, and a line carrying less than 48 bytes cannot use -a at all. Files written with -pbkdf2 or -iter are not supported`

For instance, Opera and Chrome store the hash in local SQLite databases; Firefox uses files ending with 'lpall.slps' - for Linux: 2nd line is interesting / base64 decode it; for Windows, see https://hashcat.net/forum/thread-2701-post-16111.html#pid16111 - and_key.itr`

[^13]: Module usage notice: `use this SQL query to extract the hashes:
SELECT user, CONCAT('$mysql', SUBSTR(authentication_string,1,3), LPAD(CONV(SUBSTR(authentication_string,4,3),16,10),4,0),'*',INSERT(HEX(SUBSTR(authentication_string,8)),41,0,'*')) AS hash FROM user WHERE plugin = 'caching_sha2_password' AND authentication_string NOT LIKE '%INVALIDSALTANDPASSWORD%';`
[^14]: Module advice notice: `When using the optimized-kernel: the length byte, the candidate, the domain name, the root that ends it and the salt share a single 55 byte block, so a candidate longer than what the domain and the salt leave of that block is never found. The pure-kernel takes the name a block at a time and does not have this limit.`

[^103]: Module usage notice: `This mode cracks the password of a Copay or BitPay wallet backup, which is an sjcl blob of the form {"iv":...,"iter":...,"ks":...,"ct":...}. The line carries the iteration count, the key size in bits, the salt, the iv and only the first 16 bytes of the ciphertext, so it holds nothing of the wallet. The password is verified against the 12 byte prefix the backup JSON opens with, {"network":", which means the inner xPrivKeyEncrypted blob of the same shape cannot be cracked here, and neither can an sjcl blob whose plaintext starts with something else. Key sizes of 128 and 256 bits are read`
[^104]: Module usage notice: `This mode reads the line of https://github.com/hashcat/hashcat/blob/master/tools/metamask2hashcat.py run with --shortdata32, which writes 32 bytes of the vault instead of the 64 that mode 26610 needs, so the line carries none of the mnemonic. The password is verified against the 32 byte prefix every HD wallet vault starts with, and a vault that does not start with that prefix cannot be cracked here`
[^105]: Example password: `hashcat01852`
[^106]: Example password: `openwall`
[^107]: Module usage notice: `This mode cracks the password of a Jetico BestCrypt container (.jbc) written by key generator 5, which is what BestCrypt 8 and 9 use. Use https://github.com/hashcat/hashcat/blob/master/tools/bestcrypt2hashcat.py to write the line. The hash id and the cipher mode together pick the mode: 128 for SHA-256 is hash-mode 37900 in CBC and 37901 in XTS, 10 for SHA-512 is 37902 and 129 for Whirlpool-512 is 37903. SHA-256 has one mode per cipher because its XTS key takes a second pass of the key derivation and its CBC key does not. AES is the only cipher the container format exposes in clear, in CBC or in XTS, and the line carries one key slot, so a container with several passwords gives one line per slot. The password enters the key generator one byte per character, so one outside ASCII is not reached`
